# Stack Coverage

If a company runs X, it needs these logs, detections and actions. The blind spot skill (`agents/blind-spot-detector/skills/stack-intake`) asks the questions, records the answers in the client's `stack.yaml`, then checks the SIEM. Source: `catalog/stack-coverage.yaml`.

## Endpoint (EDR) (S-01)

_In scope: always. Examples: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, Elastic Defend._

**Ask**

- Which EDR, and on what share of Windows, Mac and Linux machines?
- Is it in block mode with anti-tamper on, or alert-only?

**Logs**

- [ ] EDR alerts and telemetry (process, file, network) (Must have) · e.g. DeviceProcessEvents, Falcon event stream, Deep Visibility
- [ ] EDR sensor health / heartbeat (Must have) · e.g. DeviceInfo, sensor last-seen
- [ ] EDR console audit (policy, exclusions, uninstall tokens) (Must have) · e.g. Defender portal audit, Falcon audit log
- [ ] Decoy file read auditing (Must have) · e.g. EDR file-open events, Windows 4663 with SACL on decoys

**Depends on it:** Decoy files and canary credentials on endpoints and shares (A-01), Credential theft behavior on an endpoint (A-03), EDR tampering corroborated by a second signal (A-04), Machine-speed recon burst (A-13), Ransomware precursors (A-15), Any high/critical EDR alert not covered by Tier 1 (D-01), Server process spawning a shell (exploited service) (D-04)

**Actions it must support:** Isolate host via EDR (ACT-01), Kill process and quarantine file (ACT-10)

**Verify**

- [ ] EDR machine count vs. AD / IdP device count / CMDB. The difference is unmanaged machines
- [ ] Policies in detect-only or with prevention off
- [ ] Last event time for each EDR table in the SIEM

## On-prem directory (Active Directory) (S-02)

_In scope: if any on-prem AD exists, including hybrid. Examples: Active Directory, Samba AD._

**Ask**

- Is there on-prem Active Directory? How many domains?
- Are domain controller security logs in the SIEM, from every DC?

**Logs**

- [ ] Domain controller security logs (logons, Kerberos, account/group changes, log cleared) (Must have) · e.g. 4624, 4768, 4769, 4720, 4728, 1102
- [ ] AD-to-cloud sync / connector logs (Later) · e.g. Entra Connect, Okta AD agent

**Depends on it:** Canary AD accounts (honey user, honey SPN) (A-02), Kerberoasting / credential spraying (D-07)

**Actions it must support:** Disable account (ACT-04), Reset password and MFA methods (ACT-05)

**Verify**

- [ ] Count DCs sending logs vs. DCs in AD. One silent DC is a blind spot

## Cloud identity provider (SSO) (S-03)

_In scope: always. Examples: Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Ping._

**Ask**

- Which identity provider do people sign in with? Do SaaS apps go through it (SSO)?
- Which MFA methods are allowed? Are admins on phishing-resistant MFA?

**Logs**

- [ ] Sign-ins including MFA events (interactive and non-interactive) (Must have) · e.g. SigninLogs, AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs, Okta System Log
- [ ] Identity audit (MFA method, role and app consent changes) (Must have) · e.g. AuditLogs, Okta System Log
- [ ] Identity risk detections (Must have) · e.g. Entra ID Protection, Okta Identity Threat Protection

**Depends on it:** MFA fatigue burst followed by an approval (A-06), Risky sign-in or session anomaly (D-02), New MFA method or help-desk reset followed by a new device (D-03), New identity persistence (no-malware access) (D-06)

**Actions it must support:** Revoke sessions and tokens (ACT-03), Disable account (ACT-04), Reset password and MFA methods (ACT-05)

**Verify**

- [ ] Last event time for sign-in, audit and risk logs
- [ ] SaaS apps in the IdP vs. SaaS apps on the expense report / docs. Apps outside SSO keep sessions after a revoke

## SIEM and automation platform (S-04)

_In scope: always. Examples: Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Google SecOps, Elastic, Tines, Torq, AWS Step Functions, Sentinel playbooks._

**Ask**

- Which SIEM? How long is data searchable?
- Which automation platform runs response actions? Can it call the EDR and IdP APIs?

**Logs**

- [ ] Automation platform audit (every action, trigger, undo) (Collect now) · e.g. Tines audit, Logic Apps run history

**Depends on it:** Make the action library safe (undo, rate limits, audit) (F-04), Keep a containment action log ("did security do this to me?") (F-12)

**Verify**

- [ ] Last event time per source table / sourcetype
- [ ] Ingest lag (ingest time minus event time) per source

## Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) (S-05)

_In scope: if any cloud workloads. Examples: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud._

**Ask**

- Which clouds, and roughly how many accounts or subscriptions?
- Is control-plane logging org-wide, and is threat detection on in every account and region?

**Logs**

- [ ] Cloud control plane (Must have) · e.g. CloudTrail org trail, Azure Activity log, GCP Audit Logs
- [ ] Cloud threat detection findings (Must have) · e.g. GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud, Security Command Center
- [ ] Cloud identity sign-ins (Later) · e.g. IAM Identity Center, Azure portal sign-ins

**Depends on it:** Logging or security tool disabled (A-08), Canary cloud access keys (A-11), Cloud principal acting from outside its expected environment (A-12), New identity persistence (no-malware access) (D-06), Cloud enumeration burst or new admin grant (D-09)

**Actions it must support:** Revoke cloud credentials (tier-aware) (ACT-06), Restore cloud logging and security services (ACT-12)

**Verify**

- [ ] Accounts in the cloud org vs. accounts sending control-plane logs
- [ ] Regions with threat detection off

## Internet-facing and edge devices (S-06)

_In scope: always. Examples: Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco ASA / FTD, Ivanti, Check Point, Citrix NetScaler, Zscaler, Cloudflare._

**Ask**

- Which VPN, firewall and remote access products face the internet?
- Do their admin logins and config changes reach the SIEM?

**Logs**

- [ ] Edge device admin and config logs (Must have) · e.g. admin sign-ins, config commits, firmware changes
- [ ] VPN / remote access sign-ins (Collect now) · e.g. GlobalProtect, FortiClient, ZTNA logs
- [ ] WAF / load balancer logs (Later) · e.g. AWS WAF, Azure Front Door, Cloudflare

**Depends on it:** Know what's exposed to the internet (F-09), Edge device admin or config change (D-12)

**Actions it must support:** Network block (domain, IP, URL) (ACT-07)

**Verify**

- [ ] External scan or attack-surface tool vs. the inventory. Unknown internet-facing systems are the top blind spot
- [ ] Each edge device has a vendor, version, owner and log source in the inventory the triage agent reads

## Network services (DNS, DHCP, proxy) (S-07)

_In scope: always. Examples: Windows DNS, Infoblox, Cisco Umbrella, Cloudflare Gateway, Zscaler, Netskope._

**Ask**

- Where do DNS queries resolve (internal DNS, protective DNS)? Is there a web proxy?
- Can we block a domain or IP centrally?

**Logs**

- [ ] A second "host is alive" source (Must have) · e.g. DHCP leases, internal DNS queries, IdP device sign-ins
- [ ] DNS query logs (Collect now) · e.g. Windows DNS analytic, Umbrella, Route 53 Resolver
- [ ] Firewall / proxy / web gateway (Later) · e.g. Zscaler, Palo Alto traffic logs

**Depends on it:** EDR tampering corroborated by a second signal (A-04)

**Actions it must support:** Network block (domain, IP, URL) (ACT-07)

**Verify**

- [ ] A test block on a harmless domain shows up in DNS logs as blocked

## Email and collaboration (S-08)

_In scope: always. Examples: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Proofpoint, Mimecast, Abnormal._

**Ask**

- Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace? Is there a separate email gateway?

**Logs**

- [ ] Email gateway logs (delivery, clicks, attachments) (Collect now) · e.g. EmailEvents, Proofpoint TAP
- [ ] Microsoft 365 / Workspace audit log (Later) · e.g. Unified audit log, Workspace admin and Drive audit

**Depends on it:** Office or email client spawning a script host (A-05), Mass file download or external sharing in SaaS (D-11)

**Actions it must support:** Purge email from all mailboxes (ACT-08)

**Verify**

- [ ] Last event time for email and audit logs

## AI agents and connectors (S-09)

_In scope: if any agent can write or execute. Examples: Copilot Studio agents, Claude Code, ChatGPT connectors, custom agents on an agent platform._

**Ask**

- Which AI agents can send, change or run things (not just chat)? Who owns each?
- Which MCP servers, connectors or OAuth apps do they use?

**Logs**

- [ ] AI agent platform logs (prompts, tool calls, actions, connector changes) (Collect now) · e.g. platform audit log, MCP gateway logs

**Depends on it:** Inventory AI agents, their identities and their tools (F-10), AI agent doing something it shouldn't (D-13), New or unapproved MCP server, agent or AI connector (D-14)

**Actions it must support:** Revoke sessions and tokens (ACT-03), Disable account (ACT-04)

**Verify**

- [ ] Agent processes, MCP configs and AI OAuth apps seen on machines or in the IdP vs. the agent inventory

## Documentation and asset sources (S-10)

_In scope: always. Examples: Confluence, SharePoint, Notion, ServiceNow CMDB, a spreadsheet._

**Ask**

- Where do architecture docs live (wiki, SharePoint)? Is there a CMDB or asset list anyone trusts?

**Depends on it:** Build asset containment tiers (can / cannot auto-isolate) (F-02), Know what's exposed to the internet (F-09)

**Verify**

- [ ] Search the docs with every component's docs_search terms; anything found that isn't in stack.yaml goes back to the user as a question
